title: Doggcrapp Training review
summary: NH reviews Dante Trudel's DC training from online write-ups: one rest-pause top set per exercise, each body part twice every 8 days, extreme stretching, blast and cruise phases and a two-way split. He finds rest-pause a gimmick that steals tonnage from strength work, extreme stretching redundant, the split unsynergistic, and does not recommend the program.
claims: A program should be clear enough to put on paper; pages of rambling text usually signal an overcomplicated program
Claims of gaining 50 lb of muscle on a program are nonsense; even enhanced pros do not gain 50 lb of muscle a year
Intensity without volume is a misunderstanding of programming: raising volume raises intensity, the two go hand in hand
A top set rest-paused down until no reps are left is a fine finisher but does not replace working sets
Hitting each body part twice every 8 days is not high frequency; he trains legs every two days and some body parts every day
Explosive concentrics are good, but do not explode so hard that form breaks, e.g. the bar lifting off the shoulders out of the squat hole

DC rest-pause (7-10 reps to failure, 10-15 deep breaths, repeat twice) clones the top set in an artificial state of failure; it costs tonnage, makes progression harder to program and track, and is really three sets
For strength work, do your sets with 2-3 minutes rest between them instead; it is better for performance and tonnage accumulation
Rest-pause can be used on the last set of strength work if you skip back-off sets that day
One top set is not enough: after two minutes rest you can match it or nearly, proving the baseline was barely hurt
DC's 11-15 total reps per rest-paused set keeps higher reps in a high intensity window, which he concedes is a good point
Extreme stretching to expand fascia is a gimmick: the bottom of a loaded squat, dip or calf raise already stretches the muscle more than any post-set stretch
Weighted stretching helps calves because they carry bodyweight and are small; it will not work for quads, upper back or traps, which should just be trained
Body types like ectomorph do not exist; there are metabolism, leverages and limb lengths
High-rep lower-body work and giant sets already provide enough moderate cardiovascular conditioning
2 g of protein per lb of bodyweight is far too much
He opposes blast/cruise style polarization, volume or intensity days and deloads because they destroy tonnage stability; small dips from rep ranges are the only variation he allows
A program that forces 10 days of low intensity to recover is unbalanced; volume above maximum recoverable volume is wasted, like a huge surplus that only adds fat
Isolation progress looks slow only because the muscle is small; scaled to muscle size a small jump on curls equals a big jump on deadlift
Three exercises per muscle group is too few for some groups
Kneeling landmine press and incline press are shoulder-type vertical presses, not chest exercises; one top set of flyes as your only chest work will not grow a natural
Exercise menus should stay within the same tree of specificity and similar movement patterns
Close grip bench mostly works the chest, so picking it as a triceps exercise alongside flat bench doubles chest work
Vertical pulls fit well on a pressing day because they are easy to recover from
Pairing horizontal presses with deadlifts on the same day lacks synergy; never finish a day with deadlifts, they are strength work that belongs at the start
Upper and lower body should not be mixed on the same day in an upper/lower split
Not repeating an exercise for 8 days kills neurological adaptation and specificity
The DC sample omits traps, rear delts and abs
Advanced lifters should program for themselves rather than look for programs online
exercises: gimmick; use only as last strength set finisher
not suitable as only chest exercise
